contracts.semantic_clause:
### Persistent Workspace OOP Binding

A successful authorized OOP workspace bootstrap MAY establish a persistent non-secret workspace binding. Once established, the binding MUST remain discoverable to supported runtimes entering that workspace until explicitly revoked, superseded or invalidated by a verified workspace identity change. OOP is bound to the workspace, not to the lifespan of a chat. Persistence means a discoverable activation reference and independently re-established runtime context; it does not mean that a model remembers OOP forever.

The binding is an activation pointer, not a copy of OOP rules, an organizational authority or an adoption checkpoint. Workspace OOP-bound, persistent runtime adopted, session loaded and freshness current are independent facts. Resolve the persistent-runtime-to-checkpoint mapping under RUNTIME-01–RUNTIME-06; a new session does not create another adoption owner. The pointer MUST direct each runtime to resolve the current verified bootstrap/adoption state, rather than pinning a stale list of requirements or automatically adopting an available release. BOOT-03 governs consumer repository/release handling throughout installation and re-entry; authorization, compatibility and ordered migration gates remain applicable.

Discover this project's private-root topology and equivalent shared binding resources before creating any default. Prefer an existing authorized shared non-secret private resource within this project's root; `<project-private-root>/shared/organization-orchestration-protocol/workspace-binding.yaml` is only an informative example. The binding belongs to private technical state, never `operations`. Reuse a binding created by another authorized AI or human after verifying matching project/workspace identity, scope, provenance, authority and current status. Do not use another project's binding or create a second binding to bypass ambiguous or inaccessible state. Apply same-project append-oriented supersession and conflict-safe mutable metadata rules; preserve unresolved conflicting bindings and block affected activation rather than select by modification time.

The binding or resolved non-secret references MUST make reconstructible its binding ID, protocol ID, workspace identity and scope/root reference, known canonical project/repository identities, canonical operations reference when applicable, configured OOP repository/reference, bootstrap entrypoint, status, binding authority/evidence, creation and verification timestamps, activation policy and shared private reference. Explicitly unknown or not-applicable facts require a reason and next step where material; unknown required identity, authority or policy cannot support active status. Workspace identity MUST NOT depend solely on a filesystem path. Use actual stable repository/provider identities, an authorized workspace-local ID or equivalent identity evidence plus scope/root mappings; do not invent provider IDs. A moved path is reconciled against identity, while a copied binding, cross-workspace mismatch or verified identity change cannot silently retain activation authority.

| Binding state | Meaning and permitted activation |
| --- | --- |
| active | Sufficient current evidence establishes workspace identity, OOP reference, scope, binding authority and applicable activation policy; resolve entry before substantive governed work |
| suspended | Authority temporarily pauses automatic activation; preserve the binding and explicit suspension/resumption conditions |
| revoked | Explicit authorized revocation disables governed auto-activation from this binding; retained history does not reactivate it |
| unresolved | Required identity, authority, policy, reference or reconciliation is missing or conflicting; block dependent activation and obtain the missing basis |

A file's existence or an `active` label alone is insufficient. Suspension, revocation, supersession and resumption require applicable authority and attributable evidence; discovery MUST NOT silently reactivate them. A runtime may inspect/recover safely while affected governed work is blocked. Binding/adapters MUST NOT contain raw secrets in fields, URLs, prose or embedded evidence; reuse only necessary secure non-secret references. Schema shape cannot establish identity, authority or absence of every disguised secret.

### Runtime-native Activation Adapter

When the active runtime supports persistent native project instructions, workspace memory, a startup control, runtime-local configuration or equivalent capability, it MUST configure and verify, within authorized scope, a minimal runtime-owned adapter that rediscovers the workspace binding and invokes the current verified entry/bootstrap contract. A supported, authorized bound workspace MUST NOT require the user to repeat "use OOP", "check OOP" or "read bootstrap" in each future conversation. No mandatory vendor file, hosted runtime or paid infrastructure is introduced; use existing local/free capabilities and the discovered private root.

Before selecting or creating an activation pointer, the runtime MUST discover every applicable native persistent-instruction and activation mechanism for its actual environment, installed version and effective configuration under R21 and R22. Include instruction files, project memory, scoped rules, startup controls, runtime configuration and equivalent capabilities where applicable; determine exact supported names, locations, formats, scopes, discovery and precedence, enablement and consent/reload/restart prerequisites from applicable official documentation. A name or convention used by another runtime MUST NOT establish support. Inventory existing workspace integrations, including those installed by other runtimes, and assess their compatibility, ownership, effective scope, loading conditions and current binding/instruction references. Existing event controls, delivered context or another runtime's pointer MUST NOT waive this discovery.

Within existing installation/adoption authority, the runtime MUST autonomously prepare, install or reuse the necessary native instruction and activation arrangement selected under R22. Discovery of a supported mechanism MUST NOT establish its necessity or authorize its installation. Reuse an existing compatible integration only after verifying that it satisfies the receiving environment's documented contract and current workspace binding; its creator's identity alone neither establishes nor excludes compatibility. Preserve peer integrations and unrelated content; any shared mutation requires applicable ownership, coordination and authority. Complementary mechanisms require distinct necessary functions or an officially mandatory combination, not merely different names or delivery identifiers. Resolve binding and rendered-instruction locators from the authorized current project's topology and shared instruction references, never from another project's state or guessed paths; do not ask for authority already conferred for the same safe installation scope. Unsupported or unknown mechanisms and genuine authority or human-only dependencies block only their dependent work under the existing fallback and blocker contracts.

For each selected mechanism, verify actual placement, contents, effective enablement, scope and required administrative prerequisites before declaring its integration complete. Record the mechanism, applicable environment/version/configuration, official support reference, owned or authorized shared target, resolved references and administrative disposition in existing runtime-private state. A template match or successful file write alone does not establish a reachable native entry point. Native acceptance, consent and required reload/restart remain distinct facts under R21; do not introduce a separate synthetic dispatch or functionality-certification gate. At conversation entry and after relevant environment, configuration or binding changes, reconcile this inventory and repair only authorized missing or stale integration, reusing valid evidence and preserving the installation-chat wrapper freeze. Mechanisms without instruction files MUST provide equivalent minimal binding/entry discovery under the same authority and isolation requirements; the protected file-template contract below applies wherever an instruction file is used.

The adapter MUST contain activation/discovery instructions and necessary safe references, equivalent in its activation portion to: "This workspace is OOP-bound. Before substantive work, resolve its persistent OOP binding and execute the current verified conversation-entry/bootstrap protocol. Do not rely on conversation memory as authority." It MUST NOT copy the fat prompt, domain profiles or independently maintained OOP rule lists. Direct the runtime to read and verify the shared rendered view. Authorized reconciliation removes copies of the two procedures from owned activation blocks. Select the current verified bootstrap through the binding and existing eligibility/adoption gates. Future requirements are inherited through verified adoption, migration and knowledge realignment; a pointer requires replacement only when its activation content, locators or applicable host contract changes. If a migration changes the bootstrap entrypoint, realign and verify the owned adapter before claiming alignment.

Every native instruction file of a bound workspace MUST be generated from the distributed template `templates/native-instruction-pointer.md`, substituting only its binding and rendered-instruction locators; the only other permitted variation is a host-mandated prefix or directive recorded with its official documentation reference under R21. Every AI reading the file as instructions or modifying it MUST preserve the complete activation block, from `<!-- OOP activation block: begin -->` through `<!-- OOP activation block: end -->` inclusive, including headings, every instruction and the preservation instruction itself. The block MUST begin at the first byte of the file, or immediately after the exact documented R21 host-mandated prefix/directive; no other preceding content or arbitrary alteration is permitted. Generation and authorized OOP template updates or migration MAY replace the block only with the corresponding current verified rendered template, substituting only `<binding-locator>` and `<rendered-locator>` and retaining the documented R21 variation. These obligations remain subject to the applicable instruction hierarchy and confer no additional authority. Record each native instruction file's name and location in the owned scope of the runtime whose host reads it; the distribution lists no host-specific file names. Host-specific instruction filenames are informative implementation examples only. An integration required by one runtime belongs in runtime/private integration, never organizational authority or `operations`. Select the documented primary project instruction entry within the workspace; when a sufficient project-root entry is supported, use it rather than an optional private or nested alternative. A personal, override or additional instruction file requires a distinct necessary function or documented mandatory combination under R22. Non-publication preferences MUST NOT substitute a personal or wider-scope entry for a sufficient primary project entry. The file remains a technical activation pointer, not organizational definitions. Discover existing adapters before creating one and do not alter another runtime's adapter without applicable authority.

At every Conversation Entry Gate, the runtime MUST verify that its necessary adapter exists where supported, belongs to this runtime/workspace, resolves the current binding/bootstrap, is not stale or superseded and points to the current shared rendered view without either mandatory procedure, and that each recorded native instruction file equals the rendered pointer template plus its recorded variation and satisfies R22 placement and necessity. For an observed nonconforming owned file, assess the actual template, locators, R21 variation, ownership and current update/migration authority; preserve recoverable evidence and unrelated work, stage the exact current rendering at the selected sufficient target, conditionally replace only the authorized owned elements and verify its complete bytes and block position before advancing alignment. Retire misplaced or duplicate owned activation only after the replacement's required administrative prerequisites are verified; preserve unrelated content, peer integrations and recoverable evidence. A conforming file needs no replacement. Missing ownership, authority or required evidence blocks only the dependent repair; another runtime's files and historical evidence MUST NOT be rewritten. Without observed installation evidence, migration completion MUST remain unverified; confirmed absence permits a fresh installation without an invented migration. When repair is authorized, local, reversible and low-risk, it MUST self-heal missing/stale references and verify its administrative result autonomously, subject to INSTALL-13–INSTALL-17 for wrapper logic changes. Otherwise record the precise blocker and inform the user; another runtime's adapter or a successful file write cannot prove this runtime's activation.

### Global OOP Discovery Sentinel

Global discovery is conditional on the documented external necessity exception in R22; support for user-level instructions, global startup policy or an equivalent mechanism alone MUST NOT trigger an external installation. When official runtime documentation requires an external prerequisite that cannot be satisfied within the workspace, the runtime MUST configure and verify only that necessary authorized prerequisite. Where this requires a sentinel, it MUST identify the current project/workspace first, determine whether that workspace is OOP-bound and, if bound, resolve only its local binding and current verified OOP context before applicable governed work. A sufficient workspace-local arrangement MUST be used exclusively for this integration. Conversation memory is never authority and another workspace's OOP state is never reusable current state.

The global sentinel MUST contain no project-specific paths, workspace IDs, `.priv` or `operations` references, ticket IDs, project repositories, credentials, adoption checkpoints, cache/context or copied OOP rules. It discovers and delegates; it does not bind a workspace, select/adopt a version, own operations or carry project state. Future requirements flow through verified current-workspace adoption and knowledge realignment, not by copying rules into global settings.

If global startup interception is unnecessary, unsupported, unknown or outside authorized scope, retain sufficient project-local activation and record the applicable disposition without creating global configuration. Where coverage is limited, leave sufficient recovery instructions and tell the user the limitation; do not claim all old or new chats are automatically intercepted. A coverage limitation MUST NOT justify speculative external files. No paid service or tool/vendor-specific normative mechanism is required.

If detection, persistence or entry activation is unavailable or cannot be guaranteed for a supported entry path, the runtime MUST record the limitation, use the best available fallback, leave sufficient non-secret activation/recovery instructions and inform the user. Use explicit unsupported/unknown/blocked facts as applicable. It MUST NOT claim all future or reopened chats are automatically protected. A private file requires a reachable native control for automatic execution; determine support from the actual environment under R21.

### Shared mechanisms and version-neutral dispatch

Share reusable mechanisms; never share project governance state. Verified project-agnostic deterministic validators, thin runtime shims, global discovery sentinel, generic adapter support code without installation-owned active registrations, immutable protocol bytes/cache, non-secret support code and runtime capability evidence MAY be shared when their relevant identities and dependencies remain valid. Workspace binding, operations, tickets, private project state, authorization, adoption checkpoints, project evidence, handoff and proprietary project context MUST remain isolated.

The global sentinel MUST be thin, project-agnostic and version-neutral: identify current workspace → determine binding → resolve only its binding/current verified OOP context → invoke applicable entry/interaction governance. It MUST NOT hardcode a project adoption version or static normative behavior of one release. Workspaces with different verified OOP versions/content identities MAY coexist. Upgrading B MUST NOT change A's adoption or project-specific policy. Shared resources never establish another project's authority.

### Version-neutral sentinel validation

The Global OOP Discovery Sentinel profile MUST require version_neutral with the value true. Structural validation MUST reject missing/false version neutrality, project-specific path/state, adopted/project version fields and copied normative rules. The runtime MUST also semantically validate free-form instructions: reject hardcoded protocol-version dispatch even when the JSON shape is valid. Shape acceptance never replaces project-agnostic, secret-free discovery review. These are bounded preparation requirements, never separate post-installation functionality certification.

### Runtime folder and private reconciliation

At entry, discover the existing root, shared binding, relevant shared records and active runtime's directory/state. Reuse authorized shared resources created by another actor, reconcile only relevant current updates, preserve unrelated private data and NEVER reset another runtime's adoption checkpoint. Each runtime MUST verify its own identity, authorized scope/state path, binding reference, verified adopted OOP repository commit and any applicable version label, completed/pending/failed migrations, knowledge realignment, activation health and relevant operations reference. Apply required owned folder changes under migration/adoption and verify before alignment; a shared update is not an update to every runtime.

Determine organizational migration disposition independently for applicable scope: `UPDATE_APPLIED_VERIFIED`, `ALREADY_SATISFIED`, `NOT_REQUIRED`, `PENDING`, `BLOCKED` or `UNKNOWN`. `ALREADY_SATISFIED` requires verifying the canonical record and actual current state, including effects applied by another AI or human, without replay. `NOT_REQUIRED` means the reviewed descriptor/scope requires no organizational transformation, not that a required migration was skipped. OOP adoption MUST NOT claim `operations` was updated when only private/runtime state changed. Missing required evidence remains pending, unknown or blocked under the existing compatibility gate.
